title: Advanced snapping framework and indicators
description: Implement a robust, extensible snapping system for surface anchors, fractional face guides, feature/edge anchors, and clear indicator lines. This umbrella tracks architecture, staged delivery, QA, and docs for the full snapping feature set.

title: Add integration drag/snap tests for real interaction flows
description: Add integration tests covering pointer drag flows for part and group snapping across new anchor types, including indicator correctness and overlap-policy compatibility. Include regression cases from user-reported scenarios.

title: Documentation and in-app guidance for advanced snapping
description: Update docs and help content to explain new snap behaviors, indicators, and settings. Add concise in-app hints/tooltips so designers can discover center/quarter-line snaps without friction.

title: POC: Add part features for mitres, cutouts, and angled ends
description: Plan and implement a POC-quality but end-to-end capable part-feature system for Carvd Studio. The goal is to let users define fabrication operations such as mitres, bevels, compound end cuts, and rectangular cutouts/notches directly on parts while keeping all work isolated from develop on a dedicated POC branch. The implementation should follow a woodworking mental model: rectangular blank first, then operations on ends/faces/edges/corners. The epic covers domain modeling, UX, geometry/rendering, interaction math, cut list/reporting, tests, and documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Users can author end cuts and cutouts on parts using woodworking-oriented terminology; 3D previews reflect the features; project files persist them; cut lists/reporting reflect blank size plus operation instructions; all POC work remains isolated from develop.

title: Define fabrication semantics, feature taxonomy, and UX vocabulary
description: Write the implementation spec for the POC. Decide the canonical model for part features: rectangular blank plus operations vs exact arbitrary geometry. Define supported feature types for the POC (mitre, bevel, compound end cut, corner notch, edge/face cutout), canonical face/end naming, measurement references (long point/short point/offset), validation rules, and non-goals. Document how woodworkers should think about the workflow and how the UI should translate that into data. This issue is the source of truth for downstream implementation.
design: Reference spec added at .claude/docs/part-features-poc-spec.md. This locks the blank-plus-operations model, supported feature taxonomy, woodworking vocabulary, measurement semantics, validation rules, cut-list behavior, and POC non-goals for downstream beads.
acceptance_criteria: A concrete spec exists for supported operations, coordinate/anchor semantics, displayed terminology, measurement references, and rules for cut-list behavior. Downstream beads can implement without inventing semantics ad hoc.
notes: Revised the target taxonomy after review: the spec now uses a full 3D face/edge/corner model (6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners) and recommends operation-first target selection with progressive disclosure rather than ambiguous flat labels.

title: Extend validation, cut lists, diagrams, and exports for blank-plus-operations fabrication
description: Update the manufacturing/reporting pipeline to reflect the woodworking model chosen in the spec. Validation should reason about blank dimensions and any operation-specific constraints. Cut lists should continue optimizing blanks while also emitting operation instructions. PDF/CSV/diagram outputs should communicate that the blank is cut first and feature operations follow, without implying unsupported exact-shape nesting.
acceptance_criteria: Validation, cut lists, and exports remain coherent for feature-bearing parts. Reports show blank dimensions plus clear operation instructions and do not silently drop authored features.

title: Add regression tests for model migration, geometry, interactions, and reporting
description: Add automated coverage for the new feature system. Include model/migration tests, store behavior tests, geometry or rendering sanity tests where practical, interaction tests for authoring and manipulating featured parts, and cut-list/reporting regressions. Focus on the seams most likely to break because the app currently assumes simple rectangular parts.
acceptance_criteria: The highest-risk paths for feature-backed parts are covered by automated tests and regressions are detectable in CI for the POC branch.

title: Document the POC feature set, constraints, and user guidance
description: Update docs, tooltips, and changelog entries for the new part-feature workflow. Document the user-facing behavior, current limitations, fabrication assumptions, and any areas intentionally simplified for the POC. Include enough guidance that a woodworker can understand how dimensions, blank size, and operations relate.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation and in-app guidance explain how to use part features, what the POC supports, and what remains intentionally out of scope.

title: Extend part, assembly, store, and file models for feature-backed parts
description: Add a feature schema to the domain model. Extend Part and AssemblyPart with a PartFeature collection and any helper metadata required by the POC. Update project serialization/deserialization, validation, migrations, seed data, duplication/copy-paste, and store actions so feature-bearing parts persist correctly and survive all existing project workflows. Maintain backward compatibility for existing project files with no features.
acceptance_criteria: Part features are represented in types and persisted in project files and assemblies. Existing projects load unchanged. Feature-bearing parts survive add/update/duplicate/copy-paste/import/export flows without data loss.
notes: Added a future-proofing pass to the reference spec before implementation: downstream work should build a reusable feature framework with shared target/reference semantics, metadata, and per-feature parameter payloads rather than a narrowly hard-coded end_cut/rect_cut schema.

title: Build feature geometry pipeline and renderer split for non-rectangular parts
description: Introduce a geometry generation path for parts with authored features. Keep the current instanced box renderer for plain rectangular parts, and route feature-bearing parts through a cached mesh/geometry path that can render mitred ends and cutouts accurately enough for the POC. Ensure selection outlines and viewport visibility remain clear. Avoid regressing performance for ordinary box parts.
acceptance_criteria: Plain parts continue using the fast instanced path. Feature-bearing parts render with correct geometry, consistent transforms/colors, and acceptable performance for POC-scale projects.

title: Make bounds, hit-testing, camera framing, and ground contact feature-aware
description: Update any code paths that assume all parts are axis-scaled boxes for interaction support. This includes world bounds/AABB helpers, selection hit-testing fallbacks, camera framing, drag ground-contact calculations, and any other utilities that derive extents from length/width/thickness only. The POC does not need perfect per-face picking for every operation, but it must not select or frame featured parts incorrectly in obvious ways.
acceptance_criteria: Featured parts can be selected, hovered, framed, and moved without visibly broken bounds or camera behavior. Grounding and extents are derived from feature-aware geometry or equivalent accurate bounds data.

title: Adapt snapping, overlap prevention, and resize logic for feature-backed parts
description: Review the drag/resize/snap/overlap pipeline and remove hard assumptions that every part is a simple box. Decide where the POC should use feature-aware bounds vs conservative blank bounds. Preserve existing stability for ordinary parts while ensuring featured parts do not produce obviously invalid snapping or overlap results. Define any intentional limitations in the POC where exact feature-level snapping is deferred.
acceptance_criteria: Featured parts can participate in movement, snapping, overlap checks, and resizing without breaking core interaction loops. Any intentional simplifications are explicit and consistent with the fabrication model.

title: Design and implement woodworking-oriented feature authoring UX
description: Add the primary authoring UX for part features. Introduce a Shape or Operations section in the properties workflow that uses end/face/edge/corner language instead of XYZ language. Provide a small board diagram and/or viewport targeting affordances so users can select where a cut applies. Make the workflow reflect how a woodworker thinks: choose the part, choose the face/end, choose the operation, then enter dimensions or angles with immediate visual preview.
acceptance_criteria: Users can discover and author part features without understanding internal axes. The authoring flow is grounded in woodworking terminology and shows a live preview path for downstream feature types.

title: Implement end-cut features: mitres, bevels, and compound cuts
description: Ship the first feature family on top of the new model and authoring UX. Support left/right end operations for the part's length axis, including square, mitre, bevel, and compound cuts as defined in the spec. Ensure the properties UI, geometry preview, persistence, duplication, and derived measurements all work for these operations.
acceptance_criteria: A user can apply end cuts to either end of a part, preview them in 3D, edit them later, and save/load projects without loss. The UI exposes meaningful references such as long-point/short-point or equivalent spec-defined measurements.

title: Implement rectangular cutouts, corner notches, and edge notches
description: Ship the subtractive feature family for rectangular removals. Support at least corner notches and rectangular cutouts/notches anchored to meaningful faces/edges/corners per the spec. Make the authoring flow offset-driven and woodworking-friendly, with immediate preview and editability.
acceptance_criteria: Users can create and edit rectangular cutouts/notches with explicit anchors and dimensions. 3D previews are correct enough for fabrication planning and the data persists through project workflows.

title: Integrate part features with assemblies, parts list, duplication, and context flows
description: Wire feature-backed parts into surrounding product surfaces. Update assemblies/template editing, parts list summaries, selection/context interactions, and copy/duplicate behavior so feature-bearing parts behave like first-class citizens. Add concise summary strings or badges where helpful so features are visible outside the properties panel.
acceptance_criteria: Features survive assembly workflows and common part-management flows. Users can recognize that a part has authored operations from the surrounding UI, not only by opening the properties editor.

title: POC: Dedicated part cuts workspace
description: Move cut/feature authoring for parts out of the overloaded Properties panel and into a dedicated workspace, similar in spirit to assembly/template editing. Keep the project editor focused on layout/basic properties while introducing a fabrication-focused environment for operation targeting, ordering, previewing, and conflict handling on a single part.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated cuts workspace exists as the primary authoring surface for part operations. The main Properties panel is reduced to summary/entry-point responsibilities. Navigation, edit-session behavior, and follow-on implementation work are clearly sequenced in child beads.

title: Define dedicated cuts workspace UX, state model, and session contract
description: Specify the dedicated Part Cuts workspace before implementation. Define what entering cuts mode means, what part-local draft state exists, what save/cancel semantics apply, how conflict/warning states are surfaced, what remains visible from the project editor, and how this mode differs from assembly/template editing. Capture the information architecture for operation list, viewport, inspector, and header actions.
acceptance_criteria: A concrete UX/state spec exists for the cuts workspace, including entry/exit rules, single-part selection constraints, draft persistence behavior, and the division of responsibility between the main editor and cuts workspace.

title: Add Part Cuts workspace shell and navigation entry points
description: Implement the top-level Part Cuts editing mode/shell. Add navigation entry points from the part Properties panel summary and the part context menu. Introduce store/routing state for the active edited part and a dedicated workspace layout with header/back navigation, draft session lifecycle, and room for operation stack + preview + inspector panes.
acceptance_criteria: Users can open a dedicated cuts workspace from a part, see a stable shell for editing one part at a time, and return to the project editor without losing or corrupting state. Entry is blocked or clearly handled for unsupported contexts like multi-select.

title: Move operation stack authoring and ordering into the cuts workspace
description: Migrate full operation authoring out of the Properties panel and into the dedicated cuts workspace. Build the operation stack UI with add/edit/duplicate/remove/enable controls plus explicit ordering/reordering support. Keep woodworking-friendly summaries, presets, and operation numbering. Make the workspace the source of truth for managing multiple operations on one board.
acceptance_criteria: The cuts workspace can create and manage multiple operations on a part, including explicit ordering and duplication. The former full authoring UI is no longer required in the Properties panel for normal operation authoring.

title: Add spatial targeting, operation highlighting, and conflict feedback in cuts mode
description: Strengthen the dedicated cuts workspace with spatial editing affordances that do not fit well inside the Properties panel. Add target highlighting in the part preview, selected-operation emphasis, filtered valid-target interactions, and same-part conflict warnings/errors for overlapping or contradictory operations. Ensure operation ordering is visually meaningful and connected to preview results.
acceptance_criteria: Users can select/edit cuts through a focused spatial workflow in cuts mode, and conflicting operations on the same part are surfaced clearly. The preview reflects selected operations and makes feature order understandable.

title: Replace Properties authoring with compact cuts summary and edit entry
description: Refactor the main project editor to keep only a lightweight cuts summary in the Properties panel. Replace the full cuts authoring UI there with a compact summary of existing operations, status/conflict badges where relevant, and an Edit Cuts call-to-action. Ensure the same entry point is available in the part context menu and surrounding part-management UI.
acceptance_criteria: The main editor exposes cuts as a concise summary plus clear entry points into the dedicated workspace, reducing panel complexity while preserving discoverability of authored operations.

title: Add regression coverage and docs for the dedicated cuts workspace
description: Add automated coverage and user guidance for the dedicated cuts workspace. Cover navigation into/out of cuts mode, save/cancel session behavior, ordered operation persistence, summary updates in the main editor, and conflict/warning regressions. Update docs/tooltips/changelog text so users understand that fabrication editing now lives in a focused workspace instead of the general Properties panel.
acceptance_criteria: The dedicated cuts workspace is covered by automated tests across navigation, persistence, and conflict-display seams, and documentation/tooltips explain the new workflow and its POC constraints.

title: Define snap taxonomy, priorities, and indicator language
description: Specify canonical snap types (face, center-1D, center-2D, edge-to-midline, edge-to-quarterline, vertex/edge variants, equal spacing), per-axis arbitration priorities, and visual indicator semantics (color, style, label, precedence). Output is an implementation spec used by all downstream tasks.

title: Implement surface anchor snaps (center-1D, center-2D, edge-to-midline, edge-to-quarterline)
description: Add tangential surface-anchor snap detection on top of face-flush contact: center in one axis, center in two axes, edge aligned to face midline, and edge aligned to quarter-lines. Ensure these work for rotated parts and preserve smooth face-latched sliding.

title: Implement fractional face grid anchors (0/25/50/75/100)
description: Generate and evaluate virtual anchor lines on target faces at configurable fractions. Support one-axis and two-axis snap combinations and preserve existing snap arbitration behavior. Include opt-in setting for advanced fractions if needed later.

title: Build indicator rendering system for snap candidates and winners
description: Implement a consistent indicator layer for snapping: candidate vs winning lines, axis-aware styling, dashed quarter-lines, centerline markers, and short labels near cursor. Ensure indicators are non-interactive and do not interfere with raycasting or dragging.

title: Extend snap arbitration and hysteresis for advanced anchors
description: Update per-axis snap arbitration to handle new anchor snap types with stable precedence and hysteresis. Prevent oscillation between similar candidates and preserve smooth tangential slide while face-latched.

title: Add snap settings UI and presets for advanced snapping
description: Expose settings to enable/disable anchor families, adjust sensitivity, and choose indicator verbosity (winners only vs show candidates). Provide sensible presets: Simple, Precision, Layout.

title: Add performance instrumentation and budgets for snapping
description: Instrument snap detection and indicator rendering cost in drag loops. Add performance budgets and guardrails to keep interaction smooth with many parts/groups. Optimize candidate pruning and early exits where needed.

title: Comprehensive unit tests for advanced snap detectors
description: Add deterministic tests for surface anchors, quarter-lines, centerline snaps, edge/vertex interactions, and arbitration precedence. Include scenario fixtures for rotated parts and face-latched sliding without regressions.
